drugs.name: Nintedanib (Ofev)
drugs.mechanism: Intracellular tyrosine kinase inhibitor blocking VEGFR, PDGFR, and FGFR signaling; reduces fibroblast proliferation, migration, and myofibroblast differentiation, slowing pulmonary fibrosis progression
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2019 for SSc-associated ILD (SENSCIS trial). Also approved for IPF.
drugs.efficacy: Reduced FVC decline by 44% vs placebo at 52 weeks in SSc-ILD (SENSCIS trial, NEJM 2019)

drugs.name: Tocilizumab (Actemra)
drugs.mechanism: Humanized anti-IL-6R monoclonal antibody blocking both membrane-bound and soluble IL-6R, inhibiting IL-6-mediated JAK1/JAK2-STAT3 signaling and reducing inflammation and fibrosis
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2021 for SSc-ILD (focuSSced trial). First biologic approved for SSc.
drugs.efficacy: Reduced FVC decline in SSc-ILD; faSScinate trial showed mRSS improvement at 48 weeks. Preserved lung function in early dcSSc with ILD.

drugs.name: Mycophenolate Mofetil (CellCept)
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits de novo purine synthesis, selectively suppressing T and B lymphocyte proliferation; reduces inflammatory cell infiltration in skin and lung
drugs.approval: Standard of care for SSc-ILD (SLS II trial). First-line immunosuppressant for SSc. Off-label.
drugs.efficacy: SLS II trial: comparable to cyclophosphamide for FVC improvement at 24 months with better tolerability; modest skin score improvement

drugs.name: Cyclophosphamide (Cytoxan)
drugs.mechanism: Alkylating agent that crosslinks DNA, inhibiting lymphocyte proliferation; immunosuppressive effect via depletion of activated T and B cells
drugs.approval: SLS I trial demonstrated efficacy in SSc-ILD. Used for severe/progressive SSc-ILD and scleroderma renal crisis. IV or oral.
drugs.route: IV pulse monthly or oral daily
drugs.efficacy: SLS I trial: modest FVC improvement at 12 months vs placebo (2.53% predicted difference); limited by toxicity with long-term use

drugs.name: Rituximab (Rituxan)
drugs.mechanism: Chimeric anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody depleting B cells via ADCC, CDC, and apoptosis induction; reduces autoantibody production and B cell-mediated fibrosis
drugs.approval: Off-label for SSc. Promising efficacy in multiple open-label and EUSTAR registry studies for skin and lung involvement.
drugs.route: IV infusion, 2 doses 2 weeks apart, repeated every 6 months
drugs.efficacy: EUSTAR and RECOVER studies: significant skin fibrosis improvement (mRSS reduction ~10 points at 6 months); stabilization of lung function

drugs.name: Bosentan (Tracleer)
drugs.mechanism: Dual endothelin receptor antagonist (ERA) blocking both ETA and ETB receptors; reduces pulmonary vasoconstriction, vascular remodeling, and fibrosis driven by endothelin-1
drugs.approval: FDA approved for SSc-PAH (WHO Group 1). First oral ERA for PAH. Also prevents new digital ulcers in SSc.
drugs.efficacy: Prevented new digital ulcers (RAPIDS-1 trial, reduced new ulcers by 48%); improved hemodynamics in PAH-SSc; does not heal existing ulcers

drugs.name: Ambrisentan (Letairis)
drugs.mechanism: Selective ETA receptor antagonist with high affinity; blocks endothelin-1 mediated vasoconstriction and vascular smooth muscle proliferation in the pulmonary vasculature
drugs.approval: FDA approved for PAH (including SSc-PAH). Selective ETA blocking spares ETB-mediated vasodilation and endothelin clearance.
drugs.efficacy: Improved 6-minute walk distance and delayed clinical worsening in PAH; ARIES trials. Less hepatotoxicity than bosentan.

drugs.name: Macitentan (Opsumit)
drugs.mechanism: Dual ERA with enhanced tissue penetration and sustained receptor binding; blocks endothelin-1 induced vasoconstriction, vascular remodeling, and fibrosis
drugs.approval: FDA approved for PAH (including SSc-PAH). SERAPHIN trial. Improved tissue targeting vs bosentan.
drugs.efficacy: SERAPHIN trial: reduced morbidity/mortality composite by 45% in PAH; fewer drug interactions and less hepatotoxicity than bosentan

drugs.name: Sildenafil (Revatio)
drugs.mechanism: Selective PDE5 inhibitor preventing cGMP degradation; enhances nitric oxide-mediated vasodilation in the pulmonary vasculature
drugs.approval: FDA approved for PAH (including SSc-PAH). First-line and add-on therapy. Short-acting PDE5i.
drugs.efficacy: Improved 6-minute walk distance and hemodynamics in PAH; SUPER trial. Also used for SSc digital ulcers and Raynaud's phenomenon.

drugs.name: Tadalafil (Adcirca)
drugs.mechanism: Long-acting selective PDE5 inhibitor; once-daily dosing with sustained pulmonary vasodilation via NO-cGMP pathway enhancement
drugs.approval: FDA approved for PAH (including SSc-PAH). Once-daily dosing convenience. Preferred long-acting PDE5i.
drugs.efficacy: PHIRST trial: improved 6-minute walk distance at 16 weeks; also effective for SSc-associated digital ulcers in combination therapy

drugs.name: Treprostinil (Remodulin/Tyvaso/Orenitram)
drugs.mechanism: Synthetic prostacyclin analogue activating IP receptor; induces potent pulmonary and systemic vasodilation, inhibits platelet aggregation, and suppresses smooth muscle proliferation
drugs.approval: FDA approved for PAH (including SSc-PAH). Multiple formulations: IV, SC (Remodulin), inhaled (Tyvaso), oral (Orenitram).
drugs.route: IV/SC continuous infusion, inhaled, or oral
drugs.efficacy: Improved 6-minute walk distance, hemodynamics, and survival in PAH; FREEDOM and TRIUMPH trials. Especially effective in SSc-PAH.

drugs.name: Selexipag (Uptravi)
drugs.mechanism: Oral selective IP receptor agonist (non-prostanoid); prodrug metabolized to ACT-333679, which activates IP receptor on vascular smooth muscle, causing vasodilation
drugs.approval: FDA approved for PAH (including SSc-PAH). GRIPHON trial. First oral IP receptor agonist; more convenient than prostacyclin infusions.
drugs.efficacy: GRIPHON trial: reduced composite morbidity/mortality endpoint by 40% in PAH; effective in SSc-PAH subgroup

drugs.name: Prednisone
drugs.mechanism: Glucocorticoid binding to cytoplasmic GR leads to nuclear translocation, transrepression of NF-κB and AP-1 inflammatory genes; reduces inflammatory phase of SSc but must be used cautiously due to scleroderma renal crisis risk
drugs.approval: Standard of care for inflammatory SSc (myositis, arthritis, serositis). Low-dose, short-course preferred. Associated with increased renal crisis risk at doses >15 mg/day.
drugs.route: Oral, daily (tapered to lowest effective dose, typically ≤10 mg/day)
drugs.efficacy: Improves inflammatory symptoms but does not alter fibrotic progression. Risk of precipitating scleroderma renal crisis mandates careful use.

drugs.name: Methotrexate (Rheumatrex/Trexall)
drugs.mechanism: Folate antagonist inhibiting dihydrofolate reductase and AICAR transformylase, leading to adenosine accumulation with anti-inflammatory effects
drugs.approval: Off-label for SSc skin involvement. Moderate evidence for skin score improvement in early dcSSc. EULAR recommendation for skin-predominant SSc.
drugs.efficacy: Two RCTs showed modest skin score improvement (mRSS reduction ~4 points at 12 months vs placebo); no effect on lung function

drugs.name: Lenabasum (Anabasum / JBT-101)
drugs.mechanism: Selective CB2 receptor agonist that activates resolution of innate immune responses; reduces pro-fibrotic cytokine production (TGF-β, IL-6) and promotes anti-inflammatory lipid mediator production
drugs.approval: Investigational. Phase 2 RESOLVE-1 trial in dcSSc showed promise; Phase 3 did not meet primary endpoint for mRSS. Not yet approved.
drugs.efficacy: Phase 2: mRSS improvement at 16 weeks; Phase 3 RESOLVE-1 did not reach statistical significance. Ongoing research in SSc-ILD.

drugs.name: Fresolimumab (GC1008)
drugs.mechanism: Fully human pan-TGF-β neutralizing monoclonal antibody; blocks all three TGF-β isoforms, inhibiting fibroblast activation, myofibroblast differentiation, and ECM deposition
drugs.approval: Investigational for SSc. Phase 1 trial showed target engagement and TGF-β pathway suppression in SSc skin. Not yet approved.
drugs.efficacy: Phase 1: reduced TGF-β-responsive gene expression in SSc skin biopsies; trend toward mRSS improvement; limited by safety concerns (keratoacanthomas)

drugs.name: Riociguat (Adempas)
drugs.mechanism: sGC stimulator that sensitizes sGC to endogenous nitric oxide and directly stimulates sGC independently of NO; increases cGMP production, promoting pulmonary and systemic vasodilation and antifibrotic effects
drugs.approval: FDA approved for PAH (including SSc-PAH, PATENT-1 trial) and CTEPH. Unique dual mechanism (NO-dependent and NO-independent).
drugs.efficacy: PATENT-1: improved 6-minute walk distance and PVR in PAH; RISE-SSc trial for SSc-associated digital ulcers did not meet primary endpoint

drugs.name: Belimumab (Benlysta)
drugs.target: BAFF (B Cell Activating Factor / BLyS / TNFSF13B)
drugs.mechanism: Fully human anti-BAFF monoclonal antibody; neutralizes soluble BAFF, reducing B cell survival, maturation, and autoantibody production
drugs.approval: FDA approved for SLE and lupus nephritis. Investigational in SSc: Phase 2 trial and case series suggest benefit. Off-label use in refractory SSc.
drugs.route: Subcutaneous injection, weekly or IV infusion monthly
drugs.efficacy: Case series: mRSS improvement and stabilization in refractory SSc; Phase 2 trials ongoing. Reduces anti-Scl-70 and anti-centromere antibody titers.
